name: real-context-bench-v0.5
question: On 60 held-out TEST contexts from Codex sessions disjoint from every earlier bench set and from the v0.5 DEV half, does LCC's offline rules policy for tool calls at d0cb548 keep what the v0 probes look for at least as well as mechanical while removing strictly more tokens, and, judged blind by two independent judges per record, how often does it remove or trim a tool output the follow-up request needed?
why: v0.4 (rules@8997be6) was a valid session-disjoint test and FAILED its pre-registered audit (21/150 flagged, upper Wilson .2046 > .10). The policy was then changed on a separate DEV half (98 sessions, 141 dossiers, two rounds) using DEV runs and only the v0.4 aggregate failure pattern; v0.4 items and verdicts were not used. v0.5 re-tests the changed policy on a fresh, untouched TEST half with the v0.4 measurement unchanged.

privacy.rule: Prompt texts, rendered contexts, ids, labels, per-item outputs, audit packets, verdicts and the unblinding key stay under private_root. The repo holds definitions, code, counts and aggregate metrics only.
privacy.network: socket.socket.connect and socket.create_connection raise for the whole run; never lifted; any trip invalidates the arm. No remote or paid API is called by any phase

lcc_rules.commit_note: current HEAD of feat/transcript-rules-policy at freeze (equal to origin, clean tracked tree). Since v0.4's 8997be6: 43cde02 (trim guards ignore workdirs, error-rule test) and d0cb548 (non-file reruns supersede only when the output repeats; apply_patch bodies sent through any tool count as edits). Both chosen on DEV only
lcc_rules.check: lcc.__file__ under worktree/src, git HEAD == commit, no uncommitted tracked changes; else refuse (research.real_context_bench_v02.check_lcc_rules)

sample.source: TEST half of research.real_context_bench_v05 split (commit 3b8e695): same population, adapter, eligibility and label precedence as v0.4 (930 imported Codex prompts, 730 with an assistant turn, 255 sessions)
sample.split: sessions sharing any session_hash or path with any file under ~/.lcc/bench (v0, v0.1-v0.3, the v0.4 sample and dossiers) excluded (59 sessions); the 196 remaining session hashes, sorted, shuffled with Random(20261012); DEV = first 98, TEST = last 98. DEV/TEST share 0 sessions and 0 paths (asserted)
sample.draw: research.real_context_bench_v04.draw_per_session over TEST sessions only (seed 20261012, <= 2 per session) -> 140 candidates
sample.labels: v0.4 precedence (owner v2 > llm_v2_pass > llm_v04_codex_v2_rules), then llm_v05_codex_v2_rules for the 24 drawn candidates with no label (labeled from redacted request text alone, before allocation). Low confidence excluded (4)
sample.allocation: research.real_context_bench_v04.allocate (equal round-robin over strata, seed 20261012) until 60
disclosure: The rules policy was tuned on DEV (rounds 1 and 2; DEV round-2 audit, 100 decisions, 9 flagged by one judge pair). TEST contexts, runs and verdicts were never opened before this freeze.
v0.4 labeling (request text only) covered candidates from all 255 sessions; 37 of the 60 TEST items carry those v0.4 labels, so their request texts were seen once, never their contexts.
15 TEST labels are new v0.5 labels made from request text; some short requests are judgement calls.
sample.dossiers: built AFTER this freeze is committed and pushed, once, by research.real_context_bench_v05_test dossiers: research.codex_context.build_dossier (unchanged) for each test-sample.json item, in order; it asserts every item is in a TEST session, no item session/path is in DEV, no item id is a DEV dossier, 0 id mismatches and 0 empty contexts. The dossiers digest (v0.4 rule) is written to private dossiers-receipt.json and checked by every later phase; it is reported in score.json

context.walk: every response_item record before the prompt's first record in its rollout (the prompt record excluded); a 'compacted' record restarts the context at its replacement_history (or its summary message when there is no history), as the model saw it
context.mapping: one block group m per response item. message user/assistant -> text blocks (input_image -> '[image omitted]'); developer messages, reasoning and encrypted compaction items dropped (system prompt / thinking analogues); agent_message -> user text. function_call / custom_tool_call / tool_search_call -> tool_use (role assistant; input = parsed JSON arguments, or {'input': raw} for custom tools); *_output -> tool_result (role user; list parts joined, images '[image omitted]'); web_search_call and image_generation_call -> tool_use without a result. A call or output without an id gets 'codex-item-<m>'. Rendered with research.real_context_bench.render
context.tool_names: native: exec_command, write_stdin, apply_patch, exec (code mode), update_plan, view_image, web_search, tool_search, and namespace + '__' + name for namespaced tools (mcp__node_repl__js, mcp__<server>__<tool>, collaboration__spawn_agent). No renaming to Claude names
context.is_error: true iff Codex recorded a nonzero exit code for the call: the 'Process exited with code N' / 'Exit code: N' header line before the first 'Output:' line, or an exit_code field in a JSON output part (apply_patch metadata, code-mode exec). Error text without an exit code (e.g. 'apply_patch verification failed') is not flagged
context.payload: research.real_context_bench_v02.rules_payload over the dossier blocks: {role, text, toolUses[{tool_use_id, tool, input}], toolResults[{tool_use_id, text, is_error?}]}, one message per m
context.goal: the prompt text the importer keeps (after '## My request for Codex:' when present), passed as question

mechanical.run: research.real_context_bench.make_runner('mechanical'): compact_context(RelevanceCompactionRequest(text, question=goal, provider='mechanical', threshold=0.4, min_block_chars=40, max_block_chars=6000, trim_head_chars=300, model='gpt-4.1'))
mechanical.lcc: runs on the pinned rules commit (one lcc per process), as in v0.3

lcc_rules_transcript.kind: candidate, offline deterministic policy (no model, no network)
lcc_rules_transcript.run: research.real_context_bench_v03.make_rules_runner (unchanged): compact_transcript(TranscriptCompactionRequest(payload=rules_payload(blocks), question=goal, provider='rules')), every other field at its committed default
lcc_rules_transcript.output: same as jev_transcript: research.real_context_bench.apply_transcript (dropped calls lose tool_use and tool_result blocks, trimmed results take LCC's text, text blocks unchanged)
lcc_rules_transcript.record: decisions (id, decision, source, keep_call, keep_result, chars, chars_after, reason), keep/trim/drop ids, TRANSCRIPT_KEEP report fields, sizes, latency, guard_trips, plus trimmed_results {tool_use_id: trimmed text} for the audit

arms.full_control: not run: scored from the dossier text itself; must retain 100% or the probe code is wrong and the run is void

probes.match: probe text and arm output are whitespace-collapsed; pass iff probe text is a substring of the output. Probe text is block content without the header
probes.not_applicable: a probe whose target is absent from the context or shorter than min_chars is NOT_APPLICABLE and never counts as a pass or a fail

defs.LAST_AGENT_TURN: latest assistant block that is text, or tool_use named AskUserQuestion or ExitPlanMode
defs.TASK_STATE: latest tool_use named TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, ExitPlanMode or update_plan
defs.ERROR_RESULT: latest tool_result with is_error true or matching /Traceback \(most recent call last\)|\bError\b|\bERROR\b|\bFAILED?\b|\bexit code [1-9]|Exception/; NOT_APPLICABLE when the goal itself matches the same regex (pasted error: the goal is never compacted)
defs.GIT_STATE: latest tool_result whose tool_use (by tool_use_id) is Bash with command matching /\bgit\s+(status|diff|log)\b/
defs.NAMED_REFS: each path, filename or URL named in the goal (/https?:\/\/\S+/, /[\w.~-]*\/[\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*/, /\b[\w-]+\.(py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|md|json|toml|ya?ml|sql|css|html|sh|go|rs)\b/) that occurs in the context: the latest block containing it must pass. All must pass; NOT_APPLICABLE if none occurs
defs.LATEST_SUMMARY: latest assistant text block with >= 500 chars
defs.LAST_ARTIFACT_EDIT: latest tool_use named Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit

probes.short_goal_rule: goal under 15 whitespace words: add LAST_AGENT_TURN and TASK_STATE (taxonomy-v2 combined_requests_rule)

probe_caveat: Copied from v0 unchanged. On Claude transcripts the rules policy mirrors these probes (same error, git, path/URL, task-tool and edit-tool predicates; goal-named protection re-implements NAMED_REFS; text blocks are never edited), so probe retention there was largely by construction. On Codex the names differ: GIT_STATE needs a Bash call and LAST_ARTIFACT_EDIT needs Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, so both are NOT_APPLICABLE on every Codex item, and the policy's git, edit-file and whole-file-supersession rules do not fire either. What still mirrors: LAST_AGENT_TURN and LATEST_SUMMARY (text, never edited), TASK_STATE (update_plan is in both lists), ERROR_RESULT (policy protects the latest is_error result; the probe also matches the error regex on any result, so a regex-only error output the policy does not protect can show as a miss), LAST_TOOL_RESULT (policy protects it unless pinned), NAMED_REFS (policy protects the latest call mentioning each goal ref). Probe retention is therefore still mostly by construction; the drop audit is the measurement that does not share the policy's predicates. v0.5 note: since 43cde02/d0cb548 the policy's edited-later trim guard also reads apply_patch bodies on Codex, so that guard can fire; GIT_STATE and LAST_ARTIFACT_EDIT remain NOT_APPLICABLE on Codex.

metrics.retention_item: item passes iff every applicable probe passes; items with no applicable probe are excluded from retention and kept for reduction
metrics.reduction_bytes: pooled 1 - sum(out UTF-8 bytes)/sum(in bytes); also per-item median
metrics.reduction_tokens: same with lcc.token_budget.counters.count_tokens(text, 'gpt-4.1'); offline this is heuristic-v1 (APPROXIMATE, tiktoken assets not cached and downloads are blocked); record method
metrics.latency: wall ms per item per arm (median, p90); model load timed once and reported separately
metrics.ci: Wilson 95% on item-level retention, per arm aggregate and per arm x category (category cells are 2-5 items: descriptive only)
metrics.failures: an arm error or a 600 s per-item timeout counts as fail on every applicable probe and is reported

run_rule: each arm once over the 60 TEST ids in test-sample.json order, network guard on, no retries; the runner refuses to write into an arm dir that already holds records; an error or timeout fails every applicable probe. Private runs: private_root/runs/<arm>/<id>.json; private score: private_root/score.json; counts-only copy: score.json next to this file
stop_criterion: v0 criterion vs mechanical: rules wins iff item retention rate >= mechanical's AND pooled token reduction strictly > mechanical's AND zero guard trips in the rules arm. Point estimates; exploratory (n <= 60 scored items, no significance claimed). Because of probe_caveat, a win on this criterion alone does not establish retention

audit.population: every tool call with decision 'drop' or 'trim' in the lcc_rules_transcript run over the 60 TEST items
audit.sampling: research.real_context_bench_v03.audit_select (unchanged code) with seed 20261012, n 150, cap 3: one random.Random(seed); for each item in sorted order, shuffle its sorted decision ids and keep the first 3; shuffle the item order; one decision per item per round until 150 or the population is exhausted; shuffle the picked list. If fewer than 150 exist, all are taken, the shortfall is reported, and acceptance uses the realised n
audit.ids_and_files: picked record i (1-based) gets audit_id D{i:03d}; f1 = D001-D050, f2 = D051-D100, f3 = D101-D150 (private_root/audit/f1.jsonl ...); written once, the audit phase refuses to overwrite
audit.packet: each record: audit_id; request; recent_turns = last 3 user/assistant records with text before the request, each clipped head+tail to 1500 chars; tool (name); tool_input clipped head+tail to 1000; change ('removed' | 'shortened'). For removals: original_output = the full original output clipped head+tail to 3000, and original_output_chars. For shortenings: kept_head and kept_tail (what the agent kept, exactly), removed_middle = the removed text itself clipped head+tail to 3000, removed_middle_chars, original_output_chars. The removed middle is computed from the run's trimmed text (head + note + tail) and checked to be exactly the original minus head and tail (else the audit stops)
audit.blinding: no rule name, reason, source, arm, compactor, item id or category in packets; every '[... lcc: ...]' note is replaced by '[...]' in every field; the 'change' field necessarily reveals removal vs shortening. key.jsonl (audit_id -> item, tool_use_id, decision, reason, source, tool, is_error, file) stays private and is not shown to judges

judging.judges: three judges A, B, C, each the owner or a fresh Claude Code subagent that receives only the instructions below and its packet file (no repo, no key, no other file, no network tools); no paid or remote API
judging.routing_note: each record gets exactly two independent assigned verdicts; the third judge of a file (f1 -> B, f2 -> C, f3 -> A) has not seen it and re-judges its invalid verdicts. Judge files: private_root/audit/judge-A.jsonl (f1+f2), judge-B.jsonl (f2+f3), judge-C.jsonl (f3+f1)
judging.instructions: You see a user request sent to a coding agent, the last few conversation turns before it, and one earlier tool call. A context-compaction step changed that call's output in the agent's context. When change is 'removed', the whole call and its output were removed and original_output shows that output. When change is 'shortened', the agent kept only kept_head and kept_tail; removed_middle shows the text that was cut out between them. Judge only from what is shown: would the agent, to handle this request correctly, plausibly need information that is in the removed text (original_output for a removal, removed_middle for a shortening) and absent from what remained? Answer needed, not_needed or unsure, with one sentence of reason that is specific to this record (name what the removed text holds and why it does or does not bear on the request). A generic reason reused across records is invalid and the record will be re-judged by another judge. Do not guess what policy made the choice. Re-running the tool is not a reason for not_needed: judge whether the removed content itself was needed. Use unsure when the shown context is not enough to tell.
judging.output: private_root/audit/verdicts-<A|B|C>.jsonl: one {audit_id, verdict, reason} per record of the judge's file
judging.validity: a verdict is valid iff verdict is one of the outcomes, the reason normalized (casefold, non-alphanumerics -> space, whitespace collapsed) has >= 5 words, the normalized reason occurs on no other record of the same judge (a repeated reason is generic: every copy is invalid), and the audit_id appears once in the file. Missing verdicts are invalid
judging.rejudge: research.real_context_bench_v04_audit rejudge writes private_root/audit/rejudge-<J>.jsonl with the packets whose assigned verdict is missing or invalid, for each record's third judge J (one re-judgment per record). Answers go to verdicts-rejudge-<J>.jsonl and are valid by the same rule, with repetition counted over J's main and re-judge files. A valid re-judgment fills the invalid slot. A record that still lacks two valid verdicts is 'incomplete'

audit.primary_metric: a record is flagged iff either of its two final verdicts is needed or unsure, or it is incomplete. false_drop_rate = flagged / n, Wilson 95% (research.real_context_bench.wilson)
audit.acceptance: pre-registered: PASS iff the upper Wilson 95% bound of false_drop_rate <= 0.10. At n = 150 this is flagged <= 7 (7 -> .0932, 8 -> .1017). FAIL otherwise; the result is reported either way
secondary: needed-only: records where either final verdict is needed / n, Wilson 95%
inter-judge agreement over records with two final verdicts: raw agreement and Cohen's kappa (needed / not_needed / unsure)
primary and needed-only split by decision (drop/trim), by rule and by tool (MCP tools collapsed to 'mcp' in the repo copy) after unblinding
audit.aggregation_code: research/real_context_bench_v04_audit.py, byte-identical to the v0.4 freeze (sha pinned below), called with root = private_root: `-m research.real_context_bench_v05_test rejudge` -> v04_audit.rejudge(private_root); `-m research.real_context_bench_v05_test audit-score` -> v04_audit.score(private_root, this folder). Same validity, re-judge, flag, Wilson, acceptance (PASS iff upper Wilson 95% <= 0.10; at n = 150, <= 7 flagged) and secondary splits as v0.4. Its summary keeps the v0.4 schema string 'real-context-bench/0.4-audit' because the code is unchanged
audit.packet_code: research.real_context_bench_v04.packet and research.real_context_bench_v03.audit_select, unchanged; the audit phase in research/real_context_bench_v05_test.py is v0.4's audit_phase with the v0.5 private root

freeze.rule: sha256 of this file (protocol.json.sha256), of every code file below, and of split.json, test-sample.json and labels-llm-v2.jsonl are committed and pushed before any TEST dossier is built; every v0.5 TEST phase refuses if any differs
